newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market trade slow, rates steady.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market trade slow, rates steady.

text.p: Croatian money market trade was slow on Friday amid good liquidity but lenders generally kept the rates steady, dealers said.
"Supply is very strong and there are also quite a lot of term funds on offer, but this should not cause any changes in the rates," a dealer told Reuters.
She said supply overshot fresh demand for 19.4 million kuna by some 30 million.
Call money deals, struck at 10.5 percent, accounted for most of the new trade. One bank accepted a lower rate of eight percent to get rid of its surplus.
One-week interbank funds were granted at 12 percent and one-month at 15 percent.
Insurers granted one-week kuna at a steady 9.0 percent.
Thursday's overnight trade totalled 80.2 million kuna as five banks sought funds to maintain their mandatory reserves. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
